**Counts (data as of 2026-11-04, not stale):** Reports published with at least one recommendation that mentions "suicide":

- **2024:** 56 reports, with 98 matching recommendations.
- **2025:** 11 reports, with 19 matching recommendations.

**Is it growing?** These counts don't show growth. They show a drop from 2024 to 2025.

**What the counts can show:**
- Suicide is a recurring subject in OIG recommendations. In 2024 it appeared in 56 reports.
- The word appears in recommendations in both years.

**What they cannot show:**
- **A real decline or rise in OIG's attention.** OIG's interest in suicide prevention could have changed. Alternatively, report volume, inspection protocols, or the report types published could have changed. For example, a program that routinely reviewed suicide prevention might have ended or been reorganized. I didn't check which of these explains the drop.
- **Differences in how complete the years are.** Reports published in 2025 may have had fewer recommendations recorded so far. Recommendations are added as OIG publishes them, and the 2025 group still has 6 open items. Reports that haven't been tagged or processed could also be missing. I didn't verify this.
- **How central suicide is to each report.** A keyword match includes reports where suicide is only one line in a broader mental health or patient safety recommendation. It also misses recommendations that use other wording, such as "self-harm", "lethal means" or "safety planning".
- **Whether suicide prevention improved or worsened in VA.** These are counts of OIG's findings. They aren't a measure of outcomes.
- **A share of all OIG output.** I didn't compute the totals of all reports or recommendations per year. Without them, I can't say whether suicide's share changed. A drop in the count could simply reflect fewer reports overall.

**Closure status:** All 98 of the 2024 recommendations are closed as implemented, with a median of about 232 days to close. In 2025, 13 are closed as implemented and 6 are still open, with a median of about 242 days to close. The 2025 figure only covers the items that have already closed.

I can compare these counts against the total recommendations per year. I can also use the "Suicide Prevention" topic tag, though OIG tagged only about a quarter of reports with a topic. Either would help judge whether suicide's share changed.

**Source:** VA OIG public recommendations data, https://www.vaoig.gov/recommendations-all.

**The median for VBA recommendations is 179 days.** The middle half of them closed between 134 and 312.5 days.

**What it measures:** the days from a report's publication to the date OIG recorded the recommendation as closed. It covers 914 closed VBA recommendations that have a closure date.

- **Closure date:** it appears to record when OIG closed the item after reviewing evidence. That can come months after VBA did the work, so the figure is not the time VBA took to fix the problem.
- **Same-day closures:** 110 of the 914 closed on the day the report was published. These were presumably fixed beforehand, and they are included in the median.
- **Not-implemented closures:** 26 of the 923 closed recommendations (2.8%) were closed as not implemented. The 179-day median includes them.
- **Missing dates:** about 6% of closed recommendations across the dataset have no closure date on OIG's site, mostly from 2013 to 2016. They are left out of the median.
- **Open items:** 43 VBA recommendations are still open. They are not in the median. Their median age is 161 days, and the oldest is 1,567 days. 17 have been open more than a year.
- **Target dates:** a facility's target date is its own estimate. A closure after the target date doesn't show that a commitment was missed.
